title: feat(desktop): the webcam lane shows the face, plus editor and export follow-ups (NIW2-582)
body:
Follow-up to the webcam-track stack ([#437](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/437) → [#441](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/441) → [#442](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/442) → [#443](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/443) → [#444](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/444) → [#445](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/445) → [#446](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/446) → this). Linear NIW2-582. Base: `feature/niw2-576-webcam-share-protect`.

## What this does

- **The WEBCAM row shows the face.** The lane now has a filmstrip of the webcam file's own frames under the hide/custom blocks, laid out per clip like the CLIPS row. Cuts and slides follow the same source-anchored layout as the other lanes. Where the webcam has no footage (it started late or ended early), the tiles stay empty. A hidden section covers the faces with a near-opaque striped scrim, so it still reads as hidden. The row is now 44 px, the same height as CLIPS.
- **Editor follow-ups from the #444 review:** the webcam pauses while the screen buffers (P2), seeks during playback aim ahead by the time the last seek took (P7), and with the layer selected inside a custom section the inspector edits that section (P6). The outline rule is now pinned by a test (P8).
- **Export follow-ups from the #445 review:** the webcam framing uses the preview's clamps (E8), and webcam fill frames over a still screen follow the zoom instead of freezing its crop (E9). A GIF webcam fetch that throws synchronously no longer fails the export (E11). The MP4 clip loop moved out of the worker into a pure module and is tested over fakes (E10). The GIF worker gets a real wiring test (E7).
- **Session loading (W6):** a frozen pre-webcam session fixture, plus loader tests against the webcam sidecar.

## Why

In QA the owner found that the WEBCAM row looked empty unless it had a segment, so nothing told them it was the face. The review items were nits declined in the stack PRs. Each one either fixes a real (if minor) mismatch between the preview and the export, or replaces a weak test.

## What to review

1. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/use-source-thumbnails.ts:52` and `:100`: the hook now also decodes a **companion file**. It samples the same evenly spaced source times as the screen and maps them to the webcam's time (`t − startOffsetMs/1000`, the sign of `webcamTimeFor`). It drops samples outside `[0, duration)` and reports frames at source time. The cache key now includes the offset (or `source`), so the screen and webcam filmstrips of one recording never collide. An empty URL decodes nothing.
2. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/components/webcam-lane.tsx:100` + `timeline-geometry.ts:61`: one strip per clip entry. `thumbnailsForRangeWithin` leaves a tile empty when its nearest frame is more than one thumbnail spacing away, so a late-starting webcam does not borrow its first frame.
3. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/video-editor/video-editor-page.tsx:464` (the filmstrip hook) and `:1054` + `webcam/webcam-selection.ts:25`: the inspector target. With the **layer** selected and the playhead inside a visible override, the inspector shows that override. That is the same rule a drag of the bubble already follows.
4. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/components/webcam-layer.tsx:152` (seek lead) and `:179`–`:184` (waiting/stalled): decide whether a lead equal to the last measured seek (capped at 1 s, ignored under 80 ms) is the behaviour you want.
5. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/compose-frame.ts:111` + `compose-output-frame.ts:183`: the new `cameraTs`. Redactions still come from the held frame's whole span and are burned in **before** the crop, in source pixels, so the crop time cannot move them. **`WEBCAM_COMPOSE_REVISION` goes `wc1` → `wc2`** (`export-reuse.ts:56`), because E8 and E9 change what a webcam export draws.
6. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/export-worker.ts:335`: the clip loop is now a call to `export-clip-frames.ts`. The loop body moved verbatim, except that fills pass `t` as the camera time (E9).

**Safe to skim:** CSS, the tests, the spec paragraph.

## Decisions

| Item | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Lane thumbnails | Done. The existing hook is generalised with a `companionOffsetSeconds` parameter, not forked. Lane height 40 → 44 px to match CLIPS. Faces are dimmed to 70 % so the segment labels stay first. |
| P2 pause on `waiting`/`stalled` | Done. `waiting` always holds the webcam. `stalled` holds it only when the main element is below `HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`, because a stalled fetch can keep playing from its buffer, and pausing then would freeze the face while the screen plays. The webcam resumes on `playing`. |
| P6 inspector inside an override | Done (`webcam-selection.ts`). |
| P7 catch-up seek lag | Done: seek lead = last measured seek time while playing, capped at 1 s. A misprediction costs one extra resync, the same as today. |
| P8 outline rule test | Done (`webcamOutlined`, unit-tested). |
| W6 loader test + pre-PR fixture | Done. `session-before-webcam.fixture.ts` is frozen by hand from main's shape. Three page-level loader tests. |
| E7 wiring test | Done for GIF: `gif-worker.test.ts` runs the worker's message handler for real (mediabunny, composer and encoder faked). Done for the MP4 loop through E10. **Partly kept:** a two-line tripwire over `export-worker.ts` checks that `plan.webcam` reaches the composer and the clip loop. Mounting the MP4 worker in jsdom would mean faking the whole muxer (Output, CanvasSource, StreamTarget, encoders), so I did not do it. |
| E8 framing clamps | Done. |
| E9 animate the crop during fills | Done. Redaction exactness is unaffected (see review point 5). Limit: fills only exist while the face is visible, so over a still screen with the webcam hidden (or no webcam at all) the crop still holds, as before. |
| E10 worker-loop test | Done: `export-clip-frames.test.ts` (8 tests over a fake sink, the real lockstep cursor and a recording composer). Mutation-checked: removing the fill's camera time or the end-of-clip fill fails it. |
| E11 TDZ in `use-gif-export` | Done. Red first: the export never started. |
| Share fingerprint | Not changed. `whole:<hash>` carries no composer revision (#446's design), so a Share file made with `wc1` drawing would still be reused. None exist outside QA because the stack is unreleased. Left as is; say if you want the revision in it. |

## Checks

| Command (from `apps/kaipu-record`) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node_modules/.bin/vitest run` | 328 files, 3361 tests passed |
| `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json --composite false` | exit 0 |
| `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json --composite false` | exit 0 |
| `../../node_modules/.bin/oxlint .` | 0 errors (the 7 page warnings predate this branch) |
| pre-push `verify-local` (lefthook) | passed (47.9 s) on push of 1b4e0756 |

**Not verified:** none of this has run in the real app. On this machine the rule is no Electron and no Playwright, so the filmstrip's look, the buffering hold and the seek lead on real hardware, and a real MP4/GIF export with fills over a zoom, are for owner QA below.

## How to test it yourself

1. Record a take of about 30 s with the camera bubble on. Move your head, and leave the screen still for a few seconds while a zoom happens (click somewhere so auto-zoom proposes one).
2. Open it in the editor. **The WEBCAM row shows your face as a filmstrip**, at the same height as the CLIPS row.
3. Cut a piece out of the middle. The webcam filmstrip closes the gap exactly like CLIPS does: the faces next to the cut match the screen frames above them.
4. Select the webcam bubble and use "Hide webcam here". The hidden section is striped and covers the faces under it; it does not just tint them.
5. If the recording has a custom section (from an older session), select the bubble *outside* it, then move the playhead *into* it. The inspector switches to "Webcam section N · Custom", and changing Size changes only that section.
6. Play from a few points and scrub around. The face keeps in step with the screen; after a jump it should catch up in one go, not lag behind.
7. Export MP4 (Balanced). In the still-screen stretch during the zoom, the zoom should move smoothly while the face keeps moving, not jump at the next screen change. Check that any privacy region you drew still covers its area for its whole time.
8. Export a GIF of a range with the face. It shows the face like the MP4.
9. Open a recording made **before** the webcam stack that you had edited. Your edits are restored and there is no WEBCAM row.
